newsitem.title: UK: Sterling keeps footing above 2.81 marks in Europe.
newsitem.headline: Sterling keeps footing above 2.81 marks in Europe.

text.p: Sterling reclaimed its perch back above 2.81 marks by midsession in Europe, gaining fresh momentum after Germany's Ifo institute revealed its business climate index had fallen.
The west German business climate index fell to 92.4 in March from 93.6 in February, well below expectations of around 94.0.

"The Ifo numbers were much weaker than expected and that has had a negative effect on the mark," said Adrian Owens, international economist at Julius Baer Investments. At 0958 GMT sterling stood at 2.8120/30 marks versus 2.8058/68 in late Europe on Wednesday.
Earlier, a drop in the UK's March retail price inflation, showing headline RPI down at 2.6 percent in the year to March from 2.7 in February, gave sterling a brief lift.
Core, or underlying inflation, was at 2.7 percent year-on-year versus 2.9, but economists warned of the dichotomy between goods and service prices.
"While the underlying picture appears to be quite positive, underneath that there is real mounting pressure in the service sector," said Owens.
Economists also spoke of the difficulty facing the government in reaching its 2.5 percent target.
